zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 服務業放緩支撐美債，長債未跟上漲勢

週一美國恢復交易，10年期以內美債小幅上漲，長債卻再度走弱。5年期殖利率下降2個基點至4.21%，10年期降1個基點至4.48%，30年期升1個基點至4.99%。實質殖利率下降支撐中天期，愈往長端，受惠幅度愈小。

6月服務業活動與新訂單放緩，仍遠未陷入收縮，就業重回擴張，價格雖降卻仍偏高。加上供應鏈壓力減輕，資料延續偏弱非農後的政策緩解，但未消除今年再升息預期。Christopher Waller主張彈性使用前瞻指引，為Fed減少溝通的討論補充另一觀點，並非提出利率時程。

融資市場相當活躍。Welltower擴大加幣債發行，匈牙利歐元債訂單強勁，日本企業則因本地利率提高而持續境外籌資。Intrum尋求重整後首次高收益債，醫療貸款人卻面對資產出售取消與司法扣押。風險偏好改善，不代表每家公司都有同樣容易的再融資窗口。

## 服務業成長與價格放緩，就業反而改善

6月ISM服務業指數由54.5降至54.0，活動由57.7降至55.4，新訂單由57.3降至55.1，就業卻由47.9回升至51.2。價格由71.3降至67.7，仍在高檔，供應商交貨降至54.4。需求擴張較慢，招聘範圍卻改善，並非勞動市場突然失速。

紐約Fed供應鏈指數由5月修正後高於歷史平均1.81個標準差，降至1.25個標準差。運輸與交貨壓力降低，仍高於平均；與ISM價格放緩一樣，都不表示成本壓力已消失。

2年期殖利率下降1個基點至4.13%，與5年及10年期同向。2年與10年利差維持35個基點，2年與30年卻擴大2個基點至86。整週2、5、10及30年期仍上升3、7、10及13個基點，重開市的小幅反彈只收復部分跌勢。

實質殖利率以5年期下降最多，跌5個基點至1.94%；7年期降3至2.08%，10年期降2至2.24%，20年期降1至2.59%，30年期維持2.79%。10年期損益兩平通膨率增加1個基點至2.24%，抵銷一半實質殖利率降幅。通膨補償一個月仍下降12個基點，但週一沒有延續這項變化。

Waller在羅馬表示，指引可在實際調整利率前收緊金融情勢，疫情後通膨上升期間就曾發揮作用；但僵化承諾也可能限制央行因應變化。他與主席Kevin Warsh偏好較少指引的立場有所不同，並未支持固定未來路徑。稍早交換定價顯示7月升息機率25%，稍晚報導仍反映年底前至少一次升息；6月18份預測中也有9份預期2026年升息。

### 國庫券供給的投標表現不一

財政部$920億91天期標售最高得標利率3.735%，投標倍數2.58，最高利率分配比例93.49%。$790億182天期則為3.830%，投標倍數較強、達3.05，最高利率分配比例僅0.86%。兩券都按原規模完成、7月9日交割，投標分布卻明顯不同。

次級13週期殖利率上升7個基點至3.83%，17週期升2至3.87%，26週期升1至3.95%；4及8週期維持3.67%、3.72%，6及52週期各降1至3.66%、3.94%。壓力集中三至六個月，並非整條現金曲線走弱。

## 擴大發債與重整後回歸，各自爭取資金

Welltower在加拿大楓葉債市場籌C$11.5億，比原先考慮的最低C$7億多逾60%。這家高齡住宅業者發行C$7.5億5年期與C$4億7年期，後者以政府債加93個基點定價，低於初步約95個基點；36名投資人下單，金額逾該券三倍。用途包括償還債務。

充足訂單讓公司同時增加籌資、略收緊條件，也擴大美國企業加幣發債紀錄。市場吸引力最終仍取決於換匯後成本與實際資金需求，但這筆交易已具體顯示，本國投資人以外也有需求。

Intrum尋求€5.25億2031年到期優先有擔保債，為高融資成本迫使公司重整後，首次回到高收益市場。這家瑞典債務催收公司去年完成美國Chapter 11程序，並宣布SEK75億增資，稱可使去槓桿進度提前約兩年。擔保與新股本支持融資嘗試，市場如何評價修復後的資產負債表，仍待最終價格及訂單確認。

TenneT Germany為預計四部分、約4至20年期的歐元歐洲綠色債召開投資人會議，背後是€670億投資計畫。德國政府持股25.1%，三家機構合計約46%。股東支持與規範化揭露可擴大買盤，電網建設規模卻意味持續借款；全球公用事業上半年已發債逾$3,370億。

### 境外債、存款與股權轉換提供不同選擇

亞太借款人第二季美元與歐元債達創紀錄的等值$1,540億。Sony、Panasonic等日本發行人約$620億、占40%，本地殖利率提高使境外發債再換回日圓更具吸引力。區域歐元債約€370億，占兩種幣別合計28%。

高評級美元殖利率逾5%維持買方興趣，新興亞洲投資級美元利差接近55個基點。不過，日本及澳洲券常在亞洲不含日本指數之外，必須提供額外利差與息收才能吸引這類組合。企業提前因應可能升息，下半年預期大量發債，仍將測試需求。

印度銀行卻改以存款替代短期債。印度央行鼓勵較便宜、較持久的外幣存款後，截至7月2日的三個交易日沒有銀行發行可轉讓定存單。6月下半月發行降至7,080億盧比，一年期利率由5月7.96%降至6.84%。預期外幣流入逾$500億，可能減少批發市場票券供給；效果仍取決於資金能留多久及幣別成本。

MiniMax提出HK$65億零票息可轉債，2027年到期、轉換溢價25%，搭配股票出售後最高合計HK$145.4億，債券預計7月10日定價。安排降低當期現金利息，投資人仍須承擔短到期與支撐轉換的股權價值風險。

### 醫療貸款失去出售款，另有資產遭扣押

Aspen Group取消出售WellNow，貸款人原期待可取得最高$3億。約$30億貸款2027年到期前，債權人已聘法律顧問；獲利轉弱後，一筆$12億額度報89.9。預期出售款落空，使到期前的還款路徑減少。

Ardian支持的Santé Cie在檢方調查涉嫌貪腐與洗錢、扣押€4,550萬資產後，尋求法國mandat ad hoc協商程序。€8.2億定期貸款在揭露前高於面額，一度指示低至56.5，隨後回升約2美分。資產扣押與流動性壓力是已發生事件，調查本身並非有罪判定。

市政債供給較為正面。Massport計畫為波士頓洛根機場發行$8.12億債，支應$40億資本計畫，加入2026年約$80億機場發債。旅客活動改善支持信用基本面，各項計畫仍須按自身條件籌資。

公司債基金也受惠於風險偏好改善，LQD上漲0.03%、HYG上漲0.20%、JNK上漲0.17%。高收益基金表現較強，與股市上漲、波動率下降相呼應；個別借款人的貸款價格則仍明顯分化。

## 歐洲價格壓力未退，以色列再次降息

德國5月製造業訂單增加1.9%，前月修正為下降3.2%，年增6.2%。其他運輸設備暴增85%推高整體，排除大型合約則增1.0%，3至5月合計仍比前三個月少0.2%。歐元區需求較強，區外訂單卻下降。

歐元區零售量在4月修正後下降0.3%之後，5月增加0.2%。食品、飲料與菸草增0.6%，非食品僅增0.1%，汽車燃料下降。消費改善，未顯示全面加速。

生產者物價說明ECB為何不能只看低油價。歐元區與歐盟5月均增0.2%，慢於修正後4月；歐元區能源月減1.0%，非能源卻月增0.7%、年增2.8%，整體年增仍5.9%。部分成本緩解，其他項目仍持續上升。

Isabel Schnabel指出，天然氣仍比戰前貴約40%，核心通膨反應遠小於整體，高溫、萊茵河低水位與AI投資也增加潛在壓力。Pierre Wunsch認為環境較平靜、薪資溫和，必要時可採有限行動。官員已不把6月之後再升息視為必然，並未一致認定通膨問題結束。

以色列確實把通膨及地緣風險下降轉成降息。5月通膨降至1.9%後，央行降25個基點至3.5%，連續第二次、為2022年底以來最低。幕僚預估一年內通膨接近1%至3%目標中點，2027年第二季政策利率3%。匯率轉強與停火讓央行在預期活動加速下仍能放鬆，後續仍取決於通膨、成長、財政及地緣政治。

日本討論不同。策略師把日圓弱勢歸於財政、美國較高殖利率及緩慢升息，前資深匯率官員則認為繼續升息可扭轉低估。匯率方向雖有歧見，焦點仍是利差。創紀錄企業境外借款具體顯示，本地利率正在改變籌資決定，並不能直接證明日債或美債價格受到固定幅度影響。

## 匈牙利訂單強勁，阿根廷拒絕市場報價

匈牙利發行€30億，為4月政權更替後首筆國際債，2032及2037年到期各半，合計訂單逾€80億。定價為中間交換利率加80及125個基點，均比初步收緊35個基點。恢復歐盟資金與宣示歐元採用路徑支持需求。

重估之後，財政落實仍重要。新政府發現先前低估支出，示警赤字將明顯超標，年內可能另發美元債。2035年歐元債殖利率3.94%，比3月高點低近2個百分點。投資人取得的歐洲整合溢價已減少，更依賴預算及加入路徑真正實現。

阿根廷採另一策略。惠譽與標普升至B−，使相對美債利差縮近80個基點，2035年指標殖利率仍約8.6%。政府認為太貴，把國際發債排除在2026及2027年計畫之外；世界銀行擔保額度6.3%，提供較低成本比較。

該國已發約$40億本地美元債，預期以更多發行、多邊貸款及再融資，支應明年約$250億美元支付。$200億美國財政部交換額度仍可用，但須重新討論。2031年取得投資級是較遠目標，近期計畫仰賴替代流動性，而非昂貴國際公募債。

智利吸引本幣債買盤。非居民5月披索政府債持有創紀錄增加$29.3億至$202億，今年以來增36%。一年期損益兩平通膨由5月初降逾200個基點至2.33%，低於3%目標；交換反映一年內政策利率4.26%，目前4.5%。通膨放緩改善債券吸引力，披索貶值或Fed再緊縮仍可能削弱利差保護。

菲律賓仍偏向升息。通膨高於3%目標之際，央行今年已升50個基點，總裁Eli Remolona表示經濟可再承受25個基點。6月通膨預估6.5%，前值5月6.8%，財政支出如何影響成長及物價將左右決策。這仍是預測，不是已公布的6月結果。

利差交易同時呈現收益與脆弱性。2025年4月關稅宣布後，以美元借款投資雷亞爾、哥倫比亞披索及里拉組合，報酬26%；雷亞爾與披索2026年兌美元各升至少5%。MSCI新興匯率指數今年卻僅升0.2%，3月以來約跌1.5%。改用歐元、加幣及日圓融資可降低單一幣別集中，無法消除利差改變的風險。

EMB漲0.16%至$96.35，美元指數幾乎持平於100.85。穩定美元之下，匈牙利趁需求發債、阿根廷避開當前價格、智利吸引本幣流入，融資選擇並不相同。

## 晶片反彈，三星財報面對高期待

S&P 500漲0.72%、Nasdaq 100漲1.26%、半導體漲2.17%，結束連續兩個交易日下跌。VIX降3.59%至15.57，月降幅逾27%。美債溫和反彈伴隨風險偏好改善，並非全面避險。

三星即將公布業績，讓反彈背後的期待有了具體數字。分析師預估單季營業利益₩84.3兆、約$551億，營收增127%至紀錄₩169兆。DRAM均價季增逾40%，NAND逾50%。股價第二季翻倍、2026年漲逾160%，即使前五個交易日已跌近9%。記憶體價格若持續可支持現金流與資本支出，放慢時卻須面對極高市場期待。

原油當日漲跌不一，WTI跌0.20%至$68.55，布蘭特漲0.26%至$71.99，月跌幅仍24.29%、22.67%。荷莫茲運輸回升之際，沙烏地阿美把次月阿拉伯輕原油價格每桶下調$11，至較區域基準折價$1.50。這比單日期貨更具體呈現能源緩解。

中天期實質殖利率下降時，黃金漲1.03%至$4,155.10，月度仍走低。美元穩定也使新興市場沒有新增融資擠壓。整體符合眼前政策疑慮較低、需求仍穩的環境，但30年期美債下跌，說明尚未形成全面存續期間買盤。

## 接續貿易、Fed紀錄與長債標售

美國5月貿易7月7日美東08:30公布，紐約Fed 6月消費者預期11:00公布。6月16日至17日FOMC紀錄於8日14:00公布，9日08:30有失業救濟金。家庭物價預期與委員會討論，將釐清偏弱非農、較慢服務業減輕了多少近期政策急迫性。

週二標售$900億42天期、$520億364天期及$580億3年期；週三增額$390億10年期，週四增額$220億30年期，附息債7月15日交割。相對發行前交易的得標利率、投標分配及次級表現，可顯示長端只是需要短暫標售讓利，或面對更持久的需求不足。

德國工業生產7日美東02:00、歐元區服務業生產05:00公布，紐西蘭央行決策22:00接續，日本央行區域報告9日公布。實際產出與央行評估，將提供歐洲剩餘成本壓力、紐西蘭政策及日本薪資物價的新比較。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Services Slow, but the Long Bond Misses the Treasury Rally

Treasuries gained modestly through 10 years as US trading resumed Monday, while the long bond weakened again. Five-year yields fell 2 basis points to 4.21%, the 10-year eased 1 to 4.48% and the 30-year rose 1 to 4.99%. Lower real yields supported intermediate maturities, but the relief faded farther out the curve.

June services activity and new orders slowed without approaching contraction. Hiring returned to expansion, and prices remained elevated even after easing. Together with lower supply-chain pressure, the data allowed investors to reduce immediate Fed concerns after the weak payroll report, without abandoning expectations of another increase this year. Christopher Waller defended a role for flexible forward guidance, qualifying the debate over a quieter Fed rather than offering a rate timetable.

Financing markets were busy. Welltower enlarged a Canadian-dollar bond sale, Hungary attracted a heavily subscribed euro book and Japanese companies continued to borrow offshore as domestic rates rose. Intrum sought its first high-yield deal since restructuring, while healthcare lenders confronted a lost asset sale and a legal seizure. The reopening brought better risk appetite, not an equally easy refinancing window for every borrower.

## Services Hiring Improves as Growth and Prices Ease

The ISM services index fell to 54.0 from 54.5 in June. Business activity eased to 55.4 from 57.7 and new orders to 55.1 from 57.3, while employment rebounded to 51.2 from 47.9. Prices declined to 67.7 from 71.3, still elevated, and supplier deliveries eased to 54.4. Demand was expanding more slowly, but hiring breadth improved rather than echoing an abrupt labor-market break.

The New York Fed's supply-chain index fell to 1.25 standard deviations above its historical average from a revised 1.81 in May. Transport and delivery stress had eased, though conditions remained tighter than average. Neither this improvement nor the lower ISM price reading meant that the cost pressure had disappeared.

Two-year yields fell 1 basis point to 4.13%, alongside the five- and 10-year gains. The unchanged 35-basis-point 2s10s slope contrasted with a 2-basis-point widening in 2s30s to 86. Weekly yield increases still totaled 3, 7, 10 and 13 basis points at two, five, 10 and 30 years, respectively. The modest reopening rally recovered only a fraction of the earlier losses.

The real-yield move was strongest at five years, down 5 basis points to 1.94%. Seven years fell 3 to 2.08%, 10 years declined 2 to 2.24%, 20 years eased 1 to 2.59% and 30 years held at 2.79%. At 10 years, a 1-basis-point increase in breakeven inflation to 2.24% offset half the real-yield decline. Breakevens were still 12 basis points lower over a month, but Monday did not extend that fall.

Waller argued that guidance could tighten financial conditions before an actual policy move, as it had during the pandemic-era inflation surge, while rigid promises could constrain the Fed when circumstances changed. His remarks in Rome contrasted with Chair Kevin Warsh's preference for less guidance, without endorsing a fixed future path. Early swaps pricing put July hike odds at 25%; later reporting still showed at least one increase priced for the year. Nine of the 18 June projections also anticipated a 2026 increase.

### Bill Supply Draws Uneven Demand

Treasury's $92 billion 91-day sale stopped at 3.735%, with 2.58 bid-to-cover and 93.49% allotted at the high. The $79 billion 182-day issue cleared at 3.830%, with stronger 3.05 coverage and just 0.86% allotted at the high. Both were sold at the announced size and settle July 9, despite markedly different bidding distributions.

Secondary 13-week yields rose 7 basis points to 3.83%, 17 weeks added 2 to 3.87% and 26 weeks increased 1 to 3.95%. Four and eight weeks held at 3.67% and 3.72%, while six and 52 weeks each fell 1 basis point to 3.66% and 3.94%. Pressure was concentrated around the three- to six-month maturities rather than across the cash curve.

## Upsized Deals and Repaired Balance Sheets Compete for Capital

Welltower raised C$1.15 billion in Canada's Maple market, more than 60% above the C$700 million minimum initially contemplated. The senior-housing operator sold C$750 million of five-year notes and C$400 million of seven-year debt. The latter priced 93 basis points over government bonds versus initial discussion around 95, with orders from 36 investors exceeding three times the tranche. Proceeds included debt repayment.

The transaction converted a broad book into both more funding and slightly tighter terms. It also added to record Canadian-dollar borrowing by US companies. The attraction of that market ultimately depends on the swapped cost and funding need, but Welltower's own result showed tangible demand beyond its domestic investor base.

Intrum was seeking €525 million of senior secured bonds due 2031, its first high-yield transaction since expensive financing pushed it into restructuring. The Swedish debt collector exited US Chapter 11 last year and had announced a SEK7.5 billion equity raise, which it said could bring deleveraging forward by about two years. Security and fresh equity supported the attempted return; final price and demand had yet to establish how investors would value the repaired balance sheet.

TenneT Germany held calls for an expected four-part euro European Green Bond sale spanning roughly four to 20 years, against a €67 billion investment program. The German government held 25.1%, and three institutional owners about 46% together. Sponsorship and regulated disclosures could broaden the buyer base, but the size of the grid buildout implied recurring borrowing. Global utilities had already issued more than $337 billion in the first half.

### Offshore Bonds, Deposits and Equity Conversion

Asia-Pacific borrowers sold a record $154 billion equivalent of dollar and euro bonds in the second quarter. Japanese names, including Sony and Panasonic, accounted for roughly $62 billion, or 40%, as rising domestic yields made overseas issuance and swapping proceeds into yen more attractive. Regional euro sales reached about €37 billion, 28% of combined dollar/euro volume.

High-grade dollar yields above 5% sustained buyer interest, while EM Asian investment-grade dollar spreads were near 55 basis points. Japanese and Australian issues often fall outside Asia ex-Japan benchmarks, however, and need additional spread and carry to attract those portfolios. Expected heavy second-half issuance would keep testing that demand as companies borrowed ahead of possible rate increases.

Indian banks instead stopped issuing certificates of deposit during the three sessions through July 2 after the RBI encouraged foreign-currency deposits as cheaper, longer-lived funding. CD issuance in the second half of June fell to 708 billion rupees, and one-year rates declined to 6.84% from 7.96% in May. Expected foreign-currency inflows above $50 billion could reduce wholesale paper supply, with their durability and currency cost determining how useful the substitution would be.

MiniMax offered HK$6.5 billion of zero-coupon convertibles due 2027 at a 25% conversion premium. A concurrent share sale brought potential combined proceeds to HK$14.54 billion, with the bonds expected to price July 10. The financing lowered current cash interest but gave investors a short maturity and dependence on the equity value supporting conversion.

### Healthcare Lenders Face Lost Proceeds and Seized Assets

Aspen Group abandoned a WellNow sale that lenders had expected could raise as much as $300 million. Creditors retained legal advisers ahead of roughly $3 billion of loans due in 2027; a $1.2 billion facility traded at 89.9 after weaker earnings. Losing the prospective sale proceeds narrowed a repayment route just as maturities approached.

Ardian-backed Santé Cie sought a French mandat ad hoc after prosecutors seized €45.5 million of assets during an investigation into alleged corruption and money laundering. Its €820 million term loans, above par before the disclosure, were indicated as low as 56.5 before recovering about 2 cents. The seizure and resulting liquidity pressure were established developments; the investigation was not a finding of guilt.

Municipal supply was more constructive. Massport planned $812 million of Boston Logan airport bonds for a $4 billion capital program, joining roughly $8 billion of airport issuance in 2026. Improved passenger activity had supported sector credit fundamentals, although each program still needed financing on its own terms.

Listed credit reflected the benign broad tone: LQD rose 0.03%, HYG 0.20% and JNK 0.17%. The larger gains in high-yield funds accompanied stronger equities and lower volatility, while individual loan prices showed risks far larger than those small aggregate changes.

## Europe Retains Price Pressure; Israel Cuts Again

German manufacturing orders rose 1.9% in May after a revised 3.2% April decline and were 6.2% above a year earlier. An 85% jump in other transport equipment boosted the headline. Excluding large contracts, orders increased 1.0%, while the March–May total was down 0.2% from the preceding three months. Euro-area orders were stronger, but demand from outside the currency bloc fell.

Euro-area retail volume rose 0.2% after a revised 0.3% April decline. Food, drinks and tobacco gained 0.6%, non-food only 0.1%, and automotive fuel fell. Consumption improved without indicating a broad acceleration.

Producer prices showed why the ECB could not rely solely on cheaper energy. Euro-area and EU prices rose 0.2% in May, slower than revised April gains. Euro-area energy prices fell 1.0%, yet ex-energy prices increased 0.7% monthly and 2.8% annually; the headline annual increase was 5.9%. Relief in one component coexisted with continued cost increases elsewhere.

Isabel Schnabel said gas was still about 40% above its pre-war level and core inflation had responded much less than the headline. Heat, low Rhine water and AI investment added potential pressure. Pierre Wunsch described a calmer environment and benign wages, leaving room for limited action if necessary. Officials were no longer treating a follow-up to June's hike as automatic, but had not agreed that the inflation problem was over.

Israel did turn disinflation and reduced geopolitical risk into a policy cut. The central bank lowered its rate 25 basis points to 3.5%, its second consecutive reduction and the lowest since late 2022, after May inflation eased to 1.9%. Staff forecast inflation near the midpoint of the 1%–3% target within a year and a 3% policy rate by the second quarter of 2027. The stronger currency and ceasefire opened room to ease even as activity was expected to accelerate; officials retained conditions tied to inflation, growth, fiscal policy and geopolitics.

Japan's debate remained different. Strategists linked yen weakness to fiscal pressure, higher US yields and gradual BOJ tightening, while a former senior currency official argued that undervaluation could reverse with further hikes. The disagreement about the yen's destination still centered on the rate gap. Record offshore corporate borrowing gave a concrete example of how higher local yields were changing funding decisions, without proving a mechanical effect on either JGB or Treasury prices.

## Hungary Secures a Strong Book; Argentina Declines the Market Price

Hungary sold €3 billion in its first international deal since April's government change, split equally between 2032 and 2037 maturities. Orders exceeded €8 billion. The notes priced at midswaps plus 80 and 125 basis points, both 35 tighter than initial indications. Restored EU funding and a stated route toward euro adoption supported demand.

Fiscal delivery remained important after that repricing. The new administration signaled a substantial deficit overshoot after identifying understated spending, and another dollar issue could follow later in the year. The 2035 euro bond yielded 3.94%, almost 2 percentage points below its March peak. Buyers were now paying less for the convergence opportunity and relying more on the budget and accession path being delivered.

Argentina took a different approach. Fitch and S&P upgrades to B− helped narrow its Treasury spread by nearly 80 basis points, but its 2035 benchmark still yielded about 8.6%. The government excluded international bond sales from its 2026 and 2027 financing plan, considering those rates too expensive. A 6.3% World Bank-guaranteed facility offered a lower-cost comparison.

The sovereign had placed about $4 billion of local dollar debt and expected additional placements, multilateral lending and refinancing to cover roughly $25 billion due next year. A $20 billion US Treasury swap line remained available subject to renewed discussions. Investment grade by 2031 was a longer-term ambition; nearer term, the plan depended on alternative liquidity rather than an expensive public international issue.

Chile attracted buyers into local duration. Nonresident peso-government-bond holdings rose a record $2.93 billion in May to $20.2 billion, up 36% year-to-date. One-year breakevens were down more than 200 basis points from early May to 2.33%, below the 3% target. Swaps priced a 4.26% policy rate within a year against 4.5% currently. Disinflation improved the case for bonds, although peso weakness or renewed Fed tightening could erode the relative-rate cushion.

The Philippines retained a tightening bias. The BSP had raised rates 50 basis points during the year as inflation exceeded its 3% target. Governor Eli Remolona said the economy could absorb another quarter-point increase. June inflation was expected at 6.5% after May's 6.8%; fiscal spending's effect on growth and prices would matter to the next decision. Those were forecasts, not the released June outcome.

Carry performance showed the attraction and risk of high yields. Dollar-funded exposure to a basket of the real, Colombian peso and lira returned 26% since the April 2025 tariff announcement. The real and peso each gained at least 5% against the dollar in 2026, yet the MSCI EM currency index was up only 0.2% for the year after a roughly 1.5% decline since March. Investors' shift toward euro, Canadian-dollar and yen funding reduced concentration in one currency, without removing exposure to changing rate differentials.

EMB rose 0.16% to $96.35 and DXY was essentially flat at 100.85. That calm dollar backdrop accommodated very different funding choices: Hungary sold into strong demand, Argentina avoided the price on offer and Chile drew local-bond inflows.

## Chips Rebound Before a High-Stakes Samsung Report

The S&P 500 gained 0.72%, Nasdaq 100 rose 1.26% and semiconductors advanced 2.17%, ending a two-session decline. VIX fell 3.59% to 15.57, taking its monthly decline beyond 27%. The modest Treasury rally occurred alongside better risk appetite, not a broad flight to safety.

Samsung's coming results put numbers behind expectations for the rebound. Analysts forecast quarterly operating profit of ₩84.3 trillion, or $55.1 billion, and revenue growth of 127% to a record ₩169 trillion. Average DRAM prices had risen more than 40% and NAND more than 50% from the previous quarter. Shares doubled in the second quarter and were up more than 160% for 2026 despite a nearly 9% decline over the preceding five sessions. Sustained memory prices would support cash flow and capital spending; any slowdown would meet exceptionally high expectations.

Oil's daily close was mixed: WTI fell 0.20% to $68.55 and Brent rose 0.26% to $71.99. Monthly declines remained 24.29% and 22.67%. Saudi Aramco cut the following month's Arab Light price by $11 a barrel to a $1.50 discount against the regional benchmark as Hormuz flows recovered. That pricing change added concrete evidence of energy relief beyond the daily futures moves.

Gold gained 1.03% to $4,155.10 as intermediate real yields fell, while remaining lower over a month. Dollar stability spared EM a new funding squeeze. Together, the asset moves were consistent with less immediate policy anxiety and resilient demand, while the 30-year Treasury's loss showed that those conditions had not restored a broad duration bid.

## Trade, Fed Minutes and the Long-Bond Auction Follow

May US trade is due July 7 at 08:30 ET and the New York Fed's June consumer-expectations survey at 11:00. The June 16–17 FOMC minutes follow July 8 at 14:00, then claims July 9 at 08:30. Household price expectations and the committee's debate will help assess how far weak payrolls and slower services have reduced near-term policy urgency.

Tuesday's Treasury sales comprise $90 billion of 42-day bills, $52 billion of 364-day bills and a $58 billion three-year note. A $39 billion 10-year reopening follows Wednesday and $22 billion of 30-year bonds Thursday; coupons settle July 15. Stops against when-issued trading, bidder allocations and secondary performance will reveal whether the long end needs only a temporary auction concession or faces a more persistent shortage of demand.

German industrial production arrives July 7 at 02:00 ET and euro-area services production at 05:00. The RBNZ decision follows at 22:00, with the BOJ regional report due July 9. Actual production and central-bank assessments provide the next comparison across Europe's residual cost pressure, New Zealand policy and Japan's wage-price outlook.
